body:
### Problem

Since #32151, `tui_stop()` blocks for the full `EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS` (1000 ms) when the terminal neither answers the DA1 request (`CSI c`) nor closes stdin. The user-visible effect is that a plain `:q` / `:wq` keeps Nvim alive roughly one second longer than it should, and `$NVIM_LOG_FILE` grows a warning line per quit.

On Windows this is not a corner case here: my `nvim.log` collects that warning for a large fraction of sessions, and the delay is easy to feel when quitting (a 1 s "stall" after `:wq`).

### Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Nvim | v0.12.5 |
| OS | Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200 (x64) |
| Terminal | Windows ConPTY / conhost (also when started from a plain console window) |
| Cross-check | same v0.12.5 build for Linux, run under WSL2 with the pty harness below |
| Config | LazyVim (`--clean` behaves identically; the config is not involved) |

```
NVIM v0.12.5
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.1.1774638290
```

### Steps to reproduce (deterministic, 2 commands)

`da1pty.py` (bottom of this report, python3 ≥ 3.9, uses `os.waitstatus_to_exitcode`) starts Nvim on a pty and plays the terminal: it reads Nvim's output, keeps the pty slave open (so `did_eof` never fires) and never answers `CSI c` unless `REPLY=1`.

```
$ NVIM=/path/to/nvim REPLY=0 python3 da1pty.py     # terminal that ignores DA1
REPLY=False  elapsed=4144ms  (quit scheduled at 3000ms)  overhead=+1144ms  exit_code=0  DA1 requests seen at [20, 157, 3141]
nvim.log: 1 DA1 line(s)
  WRN 2026-09-11T13:02:06.903 ui/c/nvim  tui_stop:658: TUI: timed out waiting for DA1 response

$ NVIM=/path/to/nvim REPLY=1 python3 da1pty.py     # terminal that answers DA1
REPLY=True  elapsed=3125ms  (quit scheduled at 3000ms)  overhead=+125ms  exit_code=0  DA1 requests seen at [5, 134, 3124]
nvim.log: 0 DA1 line(s)
```

The two runs are identical except that the DA1 request sent at exit (seen at t=3141 ms / t=3124 ms) is answered in the second one: **+1019 ms**, i.e. exactly `EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS`.

#### Reproduction standard / acceptance criteria

| | overhead = `elapsed − quit_scheduled` | `nvim.log` DA1 lines |
|---|---|---|
| terminal answers DA1 (`REPLY=1`) | ~100–150 ms | 0 |
| terminal ignores DA1 (`REPLY=0`) | ~1100–1150 ms | exactly 1 per run |

* Repeat runs (2× per mode): `4128 / 4144 ms` vs `3121 / 3125 ms` — the +1000 ms band is stable.
* Pinning down the trigger needs nothing more than the exit-time DA1 request being unanswered; the two startup queries at t≈5–20 ms and t≈134–157 ms are irrelevant (they never block).

### On Windows without any harness

* `%LOCALAPPDATA%\nvim-data\nvim.log`: **324** × `tui_stop:658: TUI: timed out waiting for DA1 response` across **492** TUI sessions. The line is only written when the reply did not arrive within 1 s; a reply that arrives late but within the timeout also delays the exit, silently.
* One instrumented quit wrote the warning for its own PID, with the TUI stop logged **4620 ms after process start** — that is ~450 ms startup + a 3000 ms scheduled quit + ~1170 ms spent inside `tui_stop()` (start `12:37:44.447` → `tui_stop` `12:37:49.067`).
* The save itself is not the bottleneck: `BufWritePre`→`BufWritePost` for an 80-byte file is **3.6 ms** with `nvim --clean` and **8.9–14.3 ms** with the full config; 6 consecutive quits where the DA1 reply *did* arrive measured 3140–3158 ms for a 3000 ms schedule.

### Expected

`:q` / `:wq` does not wait on the terminal, or at least does not pay the full timeout, when the terminal has already shown that it does not answer terminal queries.

### Actual

Exit is gated on a blocking wait; when the terminal does not answer and stdin does not EOF, every quit costs 1000 ms.

### Root cause

`src/nvim/tui/tui.c` (v0.12.5):

* `:52` `#define EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS 1000`
* `:577-581` `terminfo_disable()` ends with `out(tui, S_LEN("\x1b[c")); flush_buf(tui);`
* `:654-658`

```c
  LOOP_PROCESS_EVENTS_UNTIL(tui->loop, tui->loop->events, EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS,
                            tui->stopped || tui->input.read_stream.did_eof);
  if (!tui->stopped && !tui->input.read_stream.did_eof) {
    WLOG("TUI: timed out waiting for DA1 response");
  }
```

Master has the same structure (`EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS` at `:56`, wait at `:770-773`).

### Possible fix

* Skip the wait when the terminal has not answered any of the startup queries (`CSI ? u` + `CSI c`, DECRQM): with no evidence that the terminal speaks query responses, the wait can only ever be a fixed 1000 ms penalty, because #32151's goal ("know the terminal consumed the mode-disable sequences") is unreachable.
* Or keep the wait but make it non-blocking for interactive exits (`:q`/`:wq`), or bound it by how long the terminal needed to answer the startup queries.
* Or, regardless of the above, surface the timeout to the user, as @justinmk suggested in #32151 ("we could print something like this if the timeout is reached"), instead of only a `WLOG`.

### References

* #32151 — introduced the DA1 wait (`fix(tui): ensure all pending escape sequences are processed before exiting)`); #33574 is its 0.11 backport.
* #35744 — follow-up regression ("When terminal closes, neovim closes later"); the `did_eof` term is what covers that case, but it does not help when stdin stays open.
* #31885, #32769 — the bugs #32151 was meant to fix.
* #28611 — related ~1 s hang on Windows through the OSC52 query path (the same "wait for a terminal response" pattern).
* #33599 — `TUI already stopped (race?)`.

<details>
<summary>da1pty.py</summary>

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce the nvim TUI-exit DA1 wait.

The parent process plays the terminal: it reads nvim's output, keeps the pty
slave open (so nvim's stdin never hits EOF) and never answers `CSI c` (DA1)
unless REPLY=1.

    REPLY=0 python3 da1pty.py   # terminal that ignores DA1
    REPLY=1 python3 da1pty.py   # terminal that answers DA1 promptly
"""
import os
import pty
import select
import time

NVIM = os.environ.get("NVIM", os.path.expanduser("~/nvim/bin/nvim"))
REPLY = os.environ.get("REPLY", "0") == "1"
QUIT_MS = int(os.environ.get("QUIT_MS", "3000"))
LOG = "/tmp/nvlog-da1.txt"
PROBE = "/tmp/probe.tex"
DA1_REPLY = b"\x1b[?62;4;6;9;15;18;21;22;29;52c"

open(PROBE, "w").write("probe\n")
try:
    os.remove(LOG)
except OSError:
    pass

pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    os.environ["NVIM_LOG_FILE"] = LOG
    os.execv(
        NVIM,
        [
            NVIM,
            "--clean",
            "-n",
            "--cmd",
            'lua vim.defer_fn(function() vim.cmd("qall!") end, %d)' % QUIT_MS,
            PROBE,
        ],
    )

t0 = time.time()
queries = []
status = None
while True:
    r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.02)
    if r:
        try:
            data = os.read(fd, 1 << 16)
        except OSError:  # EIO once the child has exited
            break
        if not data:
            break
        if b"\x1b[c" in data:
            queries.append(round((time.time() - t0) * 1000))
            if REPLY:
                os.write(fd, DA1_REPLY)
    wpid, st = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
    if wpid == pid:
        status = st
        break

if status is None:
    _, status = os.waitpid(pid, 0)

elapsed = round((time.time() - t0) * 1000)
print(
    "REPLY=%s  elapsed=%dms  (quit scheduled at %dms)  overhead=%+dms  "
    "exit_code=%d  DA1 requests seen at %s"
    % (REPLY, elapsed, QUIT_MS, elapsed - QUIT_MS, os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status), queries)
)
da1 = []
try:
    da1 = [l for l in open(LOG, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") if "DA1" in l]
except OSError:
    pass
print("nvim.log: %d DA1 line(s)%s" % (len(da1), "".join("\n  " + l.rstrip() for l in da1)))
```

</details>

comment_data.body: > ### Expected > > `:q` / `:wq` does not wait on the terminal, or at least does not pay the full timeout, **when the terminal has already shown that it does not answer terminal queries.** If it doesn't answer terminal queries, is it a terminal? Also, what are you talking about? cmd/powershell respond to DA1 just fine. Can't reproduce on AWS t3.large (Windows 2022 Server). Regardless, your own testing claims out of 492 sessions, only 324 got the warning. This implies that it is responding, but dreadfully slow. If it takes that long to respond to a simple escape sequence, I can't imagine the overall experience is good at all. But I get the feeling there was no human input here anyways.

I'm on Arch Linux and was able to reproduce OPs issue, as shown below:

```bash
[jack@notepc ~]$ NVIM=/bin/nvim REPLY=0 python3 da1pty.py
REPLY=False  elapsed=4130ms  (quit scheduled at 3000ms)  overhead=+1130ms  exit_code=0  DA1 requests seen at [18, 142, 3128]
nvim.log: 1 DA1 line(s)
  WRN 2026-09-13T21:23:19.044 ui/c/nvim  tui_stop:773: TUI: timed out waiting for DA1 response
[jack@notepc ~]$ NVIM=/bin/nvim REPLY=1 python3 da1pty.py
REPLY=True  elapsed=3115ms  (quit scheduled at 3000ms)  overhead=+115ms  exit_code=0  DA1 requests seen at [4, 120, 3114]
nvim.log: 0 DA1 line(s)
[jack@notepc ~]$ nvim -v
NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1633+g85c264b7d0
Build type: RelWithDebInfo
LuaJIT 2.1.1788460057
Run "nvim -V1 -v" for more info
[jack@notepc ~]$ uname -r
7.2.3-arch1-3
[jack@notepc ~]$ uname -a
Linux notepc 7.2.3-arch1-3 #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Sun, 06 Sep 2026 13:01:04 +0000 x86_64 GNU/Linux
[jack@notepc ~]$ 
```

additional env info: kitty 0.48.2

> I'm on Arch Linux and was able to reproduce OPs issue, as shown below:

The da1pty.py script is irrelevant. It intentionally doesn't respond to DA1. A functional terminal does respond.

The original issue could have been one or two sentences without all the convoluted AI generated stuff around it. nvim blocks waiting for a DA1 response before shutdown. However, this is very intentional; if we don't wait for the terminal to process everything else, then it causes other issues (e.g. random responses sent to shell). And if the terminal takes more than a second to respond to 3 bytes, your editor must be going so slow that 1 second to quit shouldn't matter.

Edit: latency over a network connection would also do it, but then everything will still feel slow, so...

any idea for what is a functional terminal on linux? would it be kitty or something else?

edit: or maybe just try WITHOUT using the python script?
Yes, kitty is good. If you just run nvim and quit, you'll see no 1s delay.

just tried, delay is minimal

```bash
[jack@notepc ~]$ 
```
